text:
sara: paging oncall — alert: gpu-pool 'east-1a' at 100% and queue growth + throttling from routing layer. seeing steady 5k queued requests. dashboard: https://console.redwood-inference/dashboard/pools/east-1a :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260314-01 — GPU pool capacity exhaustion (autoscaler didn’t add nodes). Paging: @kai @miguel oncall.

kai: on it. i see autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts but errors: 'scale limit reached' then 429 from cloud API. attaching tail of scaler log:
```
2026-03-14T09:02:12Z scaler: want=16 current=8 max_allowed=12 error=exceeded_account_quota
2026-03-14T09:02:24Z scaler: want=16 current=8 retrying...
2026-03-14T09:03:01Z scaler: want=12 current=8 success
```

miguel: the pool config had max_size=12 for that shard after the recent autoscale policy change last night (PR #4521). looks like traffic spiked beyond that. also seeing a regression in continuous batching config — effective batch window -> 120ms -> now 450ms due to new param, reducing per-GPU throughput.

priya: confirming — deploy-bot shows rollout of "continuous-batching-tweak" at 02:41 UTC (canary -> prod) by @leo. probably combined effect: smaller headroom (max_size) + slower batching = queue pileup.

leo: yes that was my change to avoid oscillations. i increased batch_wait_ms to 450 to reduce tiny-batch overheads. didn't expect this spike pattern. i can revert.

kai: mitigation plan proposals: (1) emergency bump max_size for east-1a to 24 (if quota allows) (2) revert batching param to 120ms (3) enable model-variant fallback for heavy requests to lower-capacity instance type (mistral-7b-lite) (4) temporarily route new traffic away from east-1a. need quick triage.

miguel: priority order: revert batching param first (fastest rollback), then route traffic away + bump max_size if quota OK. fallback to smaller model is safe but needs config flip and could affect latency/quality.

sara: @kai can you try reverting batching param? @priya can you prepare a routing rule to divert 30% of traffic to eu-1 until we stabilize? @leo hold on additional changes. i'll update execs/customer-impact.

kai: reverting now. running patch revert: `kubectl set env deploy/rec-runtime BATCH_WAIT_MS=120 -n prod-east`

deploy-bot: rollout started for deploy/rec-runtime (prod-east). rollout id r-20260314-987. monitoring health.

infra-bot: cloud quotas checked: east-1 account GPU quota free=4, current allocated=8, requested extra to reach 24 would fail. can request quota increase but slow.

miguel: since quota prevents big immediate bump, we need routing and batching revert fast. also prioritization: throttle heavy streaming jobs from non-paying sandbox tenants — we can drop them to best-effort.

sara: customer-impact note: several enterprise customers reported elevated latency and 503s on generation endpoints, some timed-out embeddings jobs. CS notified high-touch customers; drafting postmortem later.

leo: revert finished. deploy-bot shows successful rollout to 8/8 pods. verifying metrics...

kai: good — batch_wait_ms back to 120. I'm seeing per-GPU throughput jump ~2.3x on the stream of long-sequence requests. queue length dropping from 5k -> 900 in 3m.

miguel: prefix cache misses spiked earlier (prefix-cache hitrate 18% -> 4%). was there a cache eviction or TTL change? check recent config: `prefix_cache_ttl` was lowered in same PR #4521 from 6h -> 30m.

priya: ugh yes that TTL change was in the same change set. that explains miss storm — clients sending repeated common prompts but cache entries expired.

sara: action items: leo revert PR 4521 entirely (it tweaked batch_wait_ms and prefix_cache_ttl). kai keep monitoring autoscaler logs and set temporary route. miguel open quota ticket with cloud infra. priya coordinate CS messages.

leo: i'll open revert PR now and mark it as emergency.

kai: routing change applied: diverting 30% traffic from east-1a -> eu-1a via routing rule `route-weight east-1a=70 eu-1a=30`

infra-bot: routing rule applied. control-plane acknowledges.

sara: we should also temporarily raise per-request token limit to block huge long-running jobs? any clients doing massive sequences?

miguel: there are a few anomalous jobs from a test harness in org-9999 producing 100k tokens/req. i've flagged and rate-limited that org until they confirm.

kai: autoscaler stabilized with routing + revert — no new scale attempts since 09:12:45Z. queue down to 320.

incident-bot: Update INC-20260314-01: mitigations applied (batching param revert, routing diversion, org rate-limit). severity reduced to partial degradation.

priya: CS update posted to high-touch customers + statuspage: https://status.redwood-inference/INC-20260314-01. noting degraded performance 09:00–09:25 UTC, partial errors 09:00–09:10.

sara: oncall handoff — @miguel you'll take post-incident monitoring for next 2 hours, @leo please follow-up with revert PR and test cases to avoid TTL/batch coupling. i'll draft incident brief.

miguel: taking handoff. monitoring GPU pool and prefix-cache hit rate. will escalate if queue > 1k again.

leo: opened revert PR #4525, linking tests to ensure prefix_cache_ttl and batch_wait_ms are validated independently.

kai: final note for postmortem: root cause = combined config regression: (a) reduced prefix cache TTL causing sudden cache-miss flood, (b) increased batch wait ms lowering throughput, (c) autoscaler constrained by conservative max_size + cloud GPU quota. single change merged too many operational knobs. recommend SAFETY: require staged canary + synthetic load test before changing batching/cache params; autoscaler should auto-bump max_size or request quota earlier.

sara: agreed. i'll include that in the incident brief. closing the live incident channel but keeping monitoring. thanks all for quick responses :clap:

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260314-01 status: monitoring -> resolved (mitigated). logs and artifacts archived.

sara: postmortem please by EOD tomorrow. include timeline, customer impact, and corrective actions.

miguel: noted. I'll capture metrics and attach graphs to the postmortem.

leo: will add test coverage and a follow-up to change review checklist.
